newsitem.title: USA: U.S., N. Korean officials meet in New York.
newsitem.headline: U.S., N. Korean officials meet in New York.

text.p: U.S. and North Korean officials met in New York on Wednesday, two days after Pyongyang agreed to take part in four-party talks on a Korean peninsula peace treaty, the State Department said.

Spokesman John Dinger said the meeting was not directly related to the four-party talks and covered such issues as North Korea's missile policy, missing U.S. servicemen in Korea and an exchange of liaison offices.

As in previous meetings with U.S. officials, famine-hit North Korea again requested further food aid. The Americans promised to consider any future appeals by international bodies "aimed at meeting demonstrated needs," Dinger said.

Although this was a stock U.S. response, Washington, which already supplied food aid worth $25 million to North Korea this year, was widely expected to send more now that Pyongyang has formally accepted the four-party talks.

Acting Assistant Secretary of State Charles Kartman headed the U.S. side and Vice Foreign Minister Kim Gye Gwan led the North Korean delegation in five hours of talks on Wednesday at the U.S. mission to the United Nations, Dinger said.

The same two officials and South Korean Deputy Foreign Minister Song Yong Shik met in New York on Monday and agreed that their countries and China would hold preparatory talks on Aug. 5 to fix details of the four-party negotiations.
The aim of the four-party talks, first proposed last year by the United States and South Korea, was to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War with a permanent peace treaty.
